name: KY-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -23 point partisan lean
Incumbent James Comer seeking re-election with a large financial advantage
Minimal Democratic challenger resources and no outside spending
Prediction markets price Comer at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Comer's incumbency and $3 million war chest against a challenger who has raised under $120,000, and markets pricing Comer near 96% all point to a safe Republican hold with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge for Williams would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent James Comer is running for re-election with every structural advantage. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds over $3 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Drew Williams has raised about $119,000 with no outside support materializing.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, but prediction markets give Comer roughly a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals leave almost no realistic path for an upset, and the forecast treats this as a safe Republican seat.
